one_line_contribution: Instead of transferring prompt text or reflection heuristics across tasks, harvest from source runs a two-parameter 'noise model' of the search — rho, the base rate at which reflection-proposed edits are true improvements, and the distribution of improvement magnitudes — and inject it as the starting belief of a spike-and-slab sequential accept/reject test that replaces GEPA's fixed-minibatch candidate evaluation, with the claim scoped as a small-budget-only Pareto gain plus an ICC measurement of how task-invariant those statistics actually are.
closest_prior_work: Three literatures jointly cover the two halves and are not engaged. (1) For the adaptive-allocation half: best-arm-identification / bandit selection of prompt candidates under a fixed evaluation budget (Shi et al., 'Efficient Prompt Optimization Through the Lens of Best Arm Identification', TRIPLE, 2024) already replaces fixed-minibatch scoring with sequential elimination in exactly this setting; the Related Work names Hoeffding races, irace and Successive Halving generically but never the prompt-optimization instantiation, which is the one a reviewer will name first. (2) For the informative-prior half: prior-guided BO (piBO/BOPrO) and meta-BO transfer surrogates (RGPE) transfer a belief about where improvement lives; the proposal dismisses these as needing a shared parametric search space, but that objection does not apply to what TAP actually transfers — a prior over the improvement variable, not over the search space, which is precisely what piBO-style methods place. (3) Most damaging: empirical-Bayes sequential testing in industrial A/B platforms fits a prior over the win base rate and the lift distribution from a corpus of past experiments and uses it to stop tests early (Deng et al., 'Continuous monitoring of A/B tests without pain', 2016, and the fat-tailed-lift literature). 'Fit a prior over (base rate of true wins, effect sizes) from historical experiments, then run sequential accept/reject' is that method verbatim; running the experiments inside GEPA rather than a web product is the domain swap the track brief explicitly says reviewers score as a modest delta. Also, the cold-start competitor is described as pure fixed-minibatch evaluation, but GEPA as published already gates on a minibatch and only then spends full validation, i.e. it already implements a crude two-stage screen — the strawman version of the main baseline weakens the novelty claim further.
strongest_objection: The only comparison that establishes the contribution is underpowered by the proposal's own numbers, and the variance reduction that the power analysis depends on is unobtainable. Baseline (iii), uninformative racing, isolates transfer from adaptivity, and baseline (iv), the online prior fit on the target's first K=15 candidates, isolates transfer from cheap local estimation. Prediction (b) puts TAP over racing at 1-3 test points and prediction (c) confines the win over the online prior to the first 40-60 rollouts, while Measurement and Noise Control states an MDE of 1.5 points at n=30 paired — so the decisive contrast sits at or below the detection threshold, which is failure mode 2 in the track brief. That MDE is itself optimistic: it rests on 'the reflection proposal stream is replayed identically across evaluation-policy conditions', but in a reflective optimizer the next proposal is conditioned on the current parent and its traces, so the moment two arms make different accept decisions — the first candidate, by construction, since that is the treatment — the streams diverge and cannot be replayed. Pairing is therefore trajectory-level, not proposal-level, and the true paired SD is closer to the ~3-point per-run test SD than the design assumes. Compounding this, risk factor (6) caps reflection at ~30 calls per run, so the online-prior baseline with K=15 warms up halfway through every run; TAP's exclusive advantage window is at most 15 candidates in a 30-candidate run, and any result in that window is a handful of accept/reject decisions per seed. A reviewer will conclude the paper is powered for the comparison it must win (cold-start GEPA) and not for the two that decide whether 'transfer' is the mechanism at all.
what_would_fix_it: Make Experiment 2 the paper and fix its statistics. (a) Six source tasks gives an ICC estimated from six clusters, whose confidence interval spans nearly the whole range; no power analysis is offered for the measurement the proposal calls decisive. Expand to 20+ task clusters, or report the ICC interval and accept that the measurement can only be descriptive. (b) rho is nonstationary within a run — it falls as the parent improves — so fitting one rho per task pools early-run and late-run candidates, inflating within-task variance and deflating the between-task ICC. As written, the central test is biased toward confirming the hypothesis, and a pooled prior can pass it while being miscalibrated at every actual search depth. Condition rho and the slab on search depth or parent quality and report the ICC at matched depth. (c) Effect sizes in raw accuracy points are not commensurable across 2WikiMultiHop F1, GSM8K exact match, MBPP pass@1 and an LLM-judged instruction set with different base rates and ceilings; normalize the slab to per-example SD units before any claim that 'three numbers' port across domains. (d) Experiment 5c measures precision of accept decisions but never recall: under a low-rho spike prior the test's failure mode is fast rejection of the rare true improvement that the evolutionary search depends on, so report the false-reject rate against probe-set ground truth and show TAP does not simply become 'reject everything faster' with progress bounded by the per-candidate cap. (e) Either power the TAP-vs-racing and TAP-vs-online contrasts directly (more seeds or more targets at the 25/50 checkpoints only) or drop the point predictions in (b) and (c) and report curves with intervals. (f) Prediction (b) demands a crossover CI narrower than the checkpoint spacing while the predicted crossover, 100-250 rollouts, already spans three checkpoints (100/200/300); zero-crossing statistics bootstrap very wide, and this prediction should be replaced by a directly measurable one. (g) Run and report an actual preprint search.
missing_baseline: A fixed-minibatch-size sweep on cold-start GEPA. The mechanism decomposition predicts that >=60% of TAP's gain comes from spending fewer rollouts per rejected candidate (5a), but simply halving or tuning the fixed minibatch size — one hyperparameter, no transfer, no adaptivity, no source runs — buys the same trade of examples-per-candidate for candidates-per-budget, and at 25-50 rollouts it is the arm most likely to match TAP. Without it the headline gain is not attributable to the transferred prior. A second, nearly as damaging omission is a generic hand-set prior arm (e.g. rho fixed at some plausible value with an off-the-shelf slab, no source harvesting at all): risk factor (1) concedes this is a live outcome — 'the contribution becomes use a sensible fixed prior' — yet it appears nowhere in the arm list, so the experiment cannot distinguish 'the harvested cross-task prior' from 'any reasonable prior'. The oracle-fit and online-fit arms bracket TAP from above and below but neither substitutes for this one.
preprint_collision: The Preprint Collision Check field is empty, and Related Work opens by conceding 'All citations unverified; literature search was unavailable.' No search was performed, so the novelty claim is unestablished rather than merely unproven — under the track's own instruction that counts as a weakness, and it is the main reason novelty is scored at 4 rather than 6. The proposal is also unusually exposed here because its neighbourhood is one where fast-moving 2024-2025 work sits directly on the mechanism: bandit / best-arm-identification allocation of evaluation budget over prompt candidates (TRIPLE, 2024) and the wave of budget-aware and early-stopping variants of GEPA/DSPy candidate evaluation that followed GEPA's 2025 release. Any of these could already contain the sequential accept/reject half; an informative empirical-Bayes prior over (win rate, effect size) fitted from prior runs is the only remaining delta, and it is a well-established technique in sequential A/B testing. At minimum, targeted searches for 'prompt optimization bandit budget allocation', 'GEPA sample efficiency early stopping', 'meta-learned prior sequential testing hyperparameter', and 'transfer prompt optimization search policy' must be run and reported before novelty can be scored above borderline.
